_: Prompts for the landing artwork. `pnpm landing:gen` renders these through the OpenAI Images API and writes WebP into apps/web/public/landing. Outputs are committed; nothing here needs a network fetch at build time.
__text: Interface lettering is taken from packages/core/i18n/locales/*.json so a picture of the product uses the product's own words: statuses are Cần làm / Đang làm / Hoàn thành (tasks.status_*), never invented synonyms. Card and message content is plausible work for a team that has agents as members. Names are Vietnamese and the same in both locales, because a screenshot of one workspace with the interface language toggled is the honest reading.
style: Soft 3D character render, matte clay-like surfaces, rounded friendly forms, gentle studio lighting with soft shadows. Every character wears a wide wraparound visor with a smooth blue-to-magenta gradient, and the visor lens is TRANSLUCENT: each character's two simple round black dot eyes, and their eyebrows, are clearly visible THROUGH the lens, sitting behind the tinted glass with a soft highlight over them. Both eyes always visible, never one. The visor must read as transparent eyewear that you can see eyes through, and must never read as an opaque blindfold, a solid band, or a mask that hides the eyes. Palette: electric blue #0b5bf5, magenta accent, pastel lavender and warm cream backgrounds. Interface panels are clean and modern with generous padding and crisp, sharp, perfectly legible lettering. No watermark, no logo, no signature, no border.

__wordmark: The visor lettering is the only place the brand name is drawn rather than rendered by the Logo component. packages/ui/brand/README.md forbids retyping the wordmark because the W's feet are custom, so treat this as set dressing on a fictional headset, not as a logo placement: it is never the official mark and nothing may crop it out of a render and reuse it.
__eyes: The visor is translucent on purpose. An opaque band over both eyes reads as a blindfold, which is the opposite of what the page says about people and agents working in the open, so the rule lives in the shared style string rather than in one prompt: every character in every image has to have visible eyes.
